questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that I chose a place where I could study something that seemed relevant for my main education. Also, I wanted it to be possible to go without the need of an airplane.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I chose to go to Oslo and I'm from Copenhagen, and things seemed pretty much the same when it comes to information pages and so on. At UiO my courses got confirmed one day before the first lecture day at the university which I found strange and confusing and I was afraid I hadn't applied for correctly. That would have been nice to know a bit earlier (that everything was in order).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of information from the Erasmus team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance with information was all god, but the Erasmus tutors were a bit disengaged and they hadn't announced the program for the introduction week, so I didn't know how much time to spend on it and what was expected from me. I didn't know what was on the programme until I showed up. And even then, I didn't know what was on the programme after lunch and so on.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's easy to find something if you look at the SiO web page - both dorms and single apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I wrote in another comment: At UiO my courses got confirmed one day before the first lecture day at the university which I found strange and confusing and I was afraid I hadn't applied for correctly. That would have been nice to know a bit earlier - that everything was in order or that I was promised to get the amount of points I was required in order to get the Erasmus grant which was very important for me and the other students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses through the steps thought at the UiO web page and then it was confirmed that I had applied. But then I was accepted only right before the start of the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I asked the student information at the faculty of humanities. They said I just had to wait. Which was probably right but still frustrating.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for more courses than needed, you can always pass unsubscribe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have two courses, one for 20 ects points and one for 10 points. The first course is two hours of lecture and three hours of instruction class - not a lot for 20 points. And the second one is two hours of instruction class. This means I only had seven hours on campus each week - that very little for a full time student! I don't mind studying a lot for my self but that requires instruction too.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say it's pretty much the same as UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At both universities they try to make the students engage a lot in the class conversation. I would say that UiO is more successful in that area - especially at the course NOR2311. But as I mentioned earlier, I only had seven hours at campus weekly which is not at all enough to discuss the texts. There is a lot of work in understanding the syllabus and it would be nice to have more time on campus (with a teacher in the same room) to ask questions and give some more instruction. But this is the same with UCPH.
